title: PSD weights raised uniform-loss reversal risk in 155 pooled ferret spine records under a fixed projection model
abstract: We computed probability bounds for loss of a positive orientation component in 155 public ferret spine records with matched structure and visual tuning. Every subset of a fixed loss count was assumed equally likely. An integer-grid subset-count method gave deterministic lower and upper bounds. At 36 losses, PSD area weights gave a reversal probability from 1.407e-8 to 2.066e-8. Equal weights gave 1.689e-25 to 2.039e-23. Starting projections were similar, at 0.215 and 0.222. PSD weighting therefore raised model risk by at least 6.9e14. Positive lower bounds also resolved rare events left unseen in an earlier Monte Carlo study. Exhaustive small cases and independent resolution checks supported the calculation. These are results for a fixed pooled table and an assumed loss process. Missing cell labels, unknown efficacy, preference errors, and absent circuit dynamics prevent neuron-level risk or transfer claims.

display.caption: Deterministic probability bounds under uniform row loss. In panel A, upper bounds are lines and shaded bands extend to lower bounds. Values below 1e-30 are clipped for display. Panel B shows lower bounds with circles and solid lines and upper bounds with crosses and dashed lines at each targeted minimum. These are conditional model risks, not biological confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Extends its fixed projection and targeted-loss study with deterministic uniform-loss probability brackets; no code or data tables reused.
Its joint-error result defines a limitation of the fixed-angle and fixed-weight analysis.
Its simulation audit motivates square-root PSD as a sensitivity rule.
